small_guidance:
- The compile error is `tl.arange(0, K)` where K=IC*KD*KH*KW=216 is not a power of 2. Round K up to the next power of two as a separate constexpr `K_POW2` (e.g. 256), use `offs_k = tl.arange(0, K_POW2)` with a `k_mask = offs_k < K`, and apply that mask when loading weights and computing indices.
- Similarly guard `BLOCK_OC` to be a power of 2 (already done) and ensure all `tl.arange` calls use power-of-2 sizes. Also pass `NSPATIAL` as an int (not float) and divide by it as float.
- Try `num_warps=8` and `num_stages=2` once compile is fixed; with N=128 programs this is plenty of parallelism.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, pooled-spatial tile), with the weight tile [OC, K] held in registers/SMEM and the input patch gathered with implicit im2col. Reuse the same loaded weight across all 8 conv points within a pool window and across multiple pool tiles per program to amortize weight loads.
- Make the kernel grid (N, pool_tile) instead of (N,) so work is distributed across SMs — currently only 128 programs leaves most of the 128 SMs underused if each program does heavy serial work. Have each program compute a tile of pooled outputs, reduce-max within the 2×2×2 window in registers, accumulate the avg-pool sum, then a second tiny kernel (or atomic add) finishes the per-N reduction and adds bias+sum.
- Fold conv bias and `/divisor` into the epilogue once per pooled cell (not per conv point). Since divisor>0, max(conv)/divisor == max(conv/divisor); divide only after the 8-way max to cut FLOPs.
